newsitem.title: USA: Continental Airlines net off in first quarter.
newsitem.headline: Continental Airlines net off in first quarter.

text.p: Continental Airlines said Thursday its first-quarter profits fell less than expected as improvements in its performance continued to attract more passengers to the discount carrier.

The company's profits fell to $74 million, or $1.13 a share, from $88 million, or $1.35 a share, in the year-ago period. Fully diluted earnings per share slid to 95 cents from $1.18, exceeding analysts' consensus estimate of 89 cents.
"Continental has re-established itself as the top performer both financially and operationally," said Continental Chairman and Chief Executive Gordon Bethune.
First-quarter passenger revenues rose 14 percent to $1.6 billion on 9 percent more capacity, while operating income increased 22 percent to $146 million, the carrier said.

Revenue per available seat mile, a measure of performance, edged up .45 cent to 10.22 cents. Continental's March load factor of 74.5 percent and its yield in February were the highest ever in the Houston-based company's 63-year history.
Costs edged up mainly due to higher fuel costs and profit-sharing, it said.

Continental said it scored a "grand slam" as the only U.S. airline to finish in the top three of all four of the U.S. Department of Transportation customer satisfaction measures for 1996 -- involuntary denied boardings, on-time, baggage handling and fewest complaints.
Continental paid $68 million in 1996 profit-sharing bonuses, about 7 percent of employees' annual salary, and gave away nine new Eddie Bauer limited edition Ford Explorers for perfect attendance.
The company said it ended the first quarter with a cash balance of $927 million, up from $657 million in 1996, well above its internal target of $750 million.
